prompt: Where must a Cloud Run container listen?
hint: An address and a port.

choices.why: Loopback answers nobody outside, and the port is the one in PORT.

choices.text: Any address, on port 443 with its own certificate
choices.why: Cloud Run terminates HTTPS; the container gets plain HTTP.

choices.text: 0.0.0.0, on the port in PORT
choices.why: Right. Requests arrive from outside the container's loopback.

choices.text: A Unix socket the platform names in K_SERVICE
choices.why: K_SERVICE is the service's name, not a socket.

prompt: A service writes each new order to a file under /tmp and reads the file back on the next request. What goes wrong on Cloud Run?
hint: Where does /tmp live, and how many instances are there?

choices.text: Each instance has its own file, gone with the instance
choices.why: Right. The next request may reach another instance, or a new one.

choices.text: The write fails, because the file system is read-only
choices.why: It is writable; that is what makes the bug quiet.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the file is smaller than the memory limit
choices.why: Size is the lesser problem; the file is not shared and does not last.

choices.text: Cloud Run copies /tmp between instances, so writes conflict
choices.why: Nothing is copied between instances.

prompt: After SIGTERM, how many seconds does a Cloud Run instance get before SIGKILL?
hint: The same as Docker's default.

prompt: An image built on an Arm laptop for Arm is deployed to Cloud Run. What happens?
hint: What does Cloud Run execute?

choices.text: It runs, more slowly, under emulation
choices.why: Cloud Run does not emulate another architecture.

choices.text: It runs at the same speed, since Python is interpreted
choices.why: The interpreter itself is an Arm binary in that image.

choices.text: Cloud Run rebuilds it for amd64 from the Dockerfile
choices.why: Cloud Run receives an image, not a Dockerfile.

choices.text: It does not start: Cloud Run executes linux/amd64
choices.why: Right. Build for amd64, or for both.

prompt: Cloud Run sets K_SERVICE, K_CONFIGURATION and K____ to name what is serving the request.
hint: Lesson 9 is about it.

prompt: Why does the orders service log one JSON object per line with a severity field?
hint: Who reads standard output on Cloud Run?

choices.text: Because Cloud Run refuses plain-text logs
choices.why: Plain text is accepted, as unstructured entries.

choices.text: Cloud Logging files each line as a structured entry
choices.why: Right. A warning stays a warning.

choices.text: JSON lines are shorter, so they cost less to store in Cloud Logging
choices.why: They are longer, if anything; structure is the point.

choices.text: Python's http.server writes JSON by default
choices.why: The program overrides log_message to write it.

prompt: What is ORDERS_DELAY_MS in the orders service for?
hint: Zero unless set.

choices.text: It sets how long Cloud Run waits before killing the instance
choices.why: That is the ten seconds after SIGTERM, which no variable changes.

choices.text: It throttles clients that send too many requests
choices.why: It delays every /orders answer equally.

choices.text: It stands in for a database call, for lesson 11
choices.why: Right. A request that waits, without a database to wait on.

choices.text: It is the startup probe's timeout
choices.why: The probe is configured on the service, not in the program.

prompt: docker image ls reported the size of orders:1. How many MB?
hint: Nearly all of it is the base image.

prompt: Why is the Dockerfile's CMD a JSON list rather than CMD python3 app.py?
hint: Which process receives SIGTERM?

choices.text: Python is then process 1 and receives SIGTERM itself
choices.why: Right. In the shell form sh gets it and does not pass it on.

choices.text: The JSON form starts Python faster
choices.why: Start-up time is not what differs.

choices.text: Cloud Run only accepts the JSON form
choices.why: Both forms run; one of them stops badly.

choices.text: The shell form cannot read the PORT variable
choices.why: A shell reads variables perfectly well.

prompt: A server inside the container listened on 127.0.0.1:8081, published with -p 8081:8081. What did curl get, and why?
hint: Which interface do published connections arrive on?

choices.text: A 404, because http.server serves no /orders path
choices.why: The request never reached a server to say 404.

choices.text: A timeout, because Docker blocks port 8081
choices.why: Docker accepted the connection and found nobody behind it.

choices.text: The directory listing, because loopback is reachable through -p
choices.why: It is not; that is the bug.

choices.text: A reset connection: nothing listened on the outside interface
choices.why: Right. Status 56, Recv failure. Cloud Run would fail its startup probe.

prompt: With CMD in shell form, docker stop took 10.227 seconds and the exit code was 137. What signal number killed it?
hint: 137 minus 128.

prompt: The orders service was started a second time with -e PORT=9090. What does that test?
hint: Who chooses the port on Cloud Run?

choices.text: Whether two copies can share one port
choices.why: They used different ports on the laptop.

choices.text: That it listens where PORT says
choices.why: Right. Cloud Run is free to choose.

choices.text: Whether the image can be rebuilt for another port
choices.why: Nothing was rebuilt; the same image ran.

choices.text: That Cloud Run only allows ports above 9000
choices.why: There is no such rule; 8080 is the default.

prompt: Put what happened when docker stop ran against the orders service in order.
hint: A signal, a handler, an exit.
items: docker stop returns, in a fraction of a second
trap: With the shell form, the second step never happens and the last one waits ten seconds.

prompt: A team's service drops a few requests every time Cloud Run scales in, and its Dockerfile ends with CMD gunicorn app:app. What is the most likely cause?
hint: Which process hears the signal?

choices.text: gunicorn cannot run on Cloud Run
choices.why: It runs; lesson 19 uses it.

choices.text: Scale-in sends requests to instances that have already stopped
choices.why: Cloud Run stops routing to an instance before shutting it down.

choices.text: The shell form: sh hears SIGTERM, gunicorn never does
choices.why: Right. Ten seconds later, SIGKILL cuts the requests in flight.

choices.text: The image is too large to be pulled during scale-in
choices.why: Scaling in pulls nothing.

prompt: A service has min_instance_count = 0 and nobody has called it for an hour. How many instances does it have?
hint: Idle instances are not kept forever.

choices.text: None; the next request waits for one
choices.why: Right. That wait is the cold start.

choices.text: One, kept warm by default
choices.why: Only a minimum keeps one; the default is zero.

choices.text: As many as the last busy hour needed
choices.why: Idle instances are shut down, after up to about fifteen minutes.

choices.text: Ten, the max_instance_count
choices.why: The maximum is a ceiling, not a target.

prompt: What is max_instance_count = 10 protecting against?
hint: What would a burst of traffic do without it?

choices.text: Instances starting before the image is pulled
choices.why: Pulling comes before starting, whatever the maximum.

choices.text: Requests waiting longer than the timeout
choices.why: A ceiling can make requests wait longer, not shorter.

choices.text: Ten requests arriving at the same instance at once
choices.why: That is concurrency per instance, a different setting.

choices.text: A burst, or an attack, scaling the bill without limit
choices.why: Right. It caps how many instances you can be charged for.

prompt: Why is the image named by an Artifact Registry path in main.tf?
hint: Where does Cloud Run pull from?

choices.text: Terraform validates the image's contents through the path
choices.why: The plan checked nothing about the image.

choices.text: Cloud Run pulls from a registry, never from your laptop
choices.why: Right. orders:1 on your laptop is invisible to Google.

choices.text: Because Artifact Registry builds the image from app.py
choices.why: A registry stores images; it does not build them.

choices.text: The region in the path sets the service's region
choices.why: location sets the region; the path only says where the image is.

prompt: With min_instance_count = ___, a single instance is always there and is billed while idle.
hint: A number.

prompt: What can this lab show about deploying the orders service? Choose all that apply.
hint: What needs Google and what does not?

choices.text: That the container keeps the runtime contract
choices.why: Right; docker run proved it.

choices.text: The service description Terraform would send
choices.why: Right; the plan is computed locally.

choices.text: The run.app address the service would get
choices.why: Only Google assigns it, and nothing is invented here.

choices.text: How long Cloud Run takes to start an instance
choices.why: A laptop timing is the laptop's, not Cloud Run's.

prompt: Put the four states of a scale-to-zero service in the order a quiet morning goes through them.
hint: It ends where it began.
trap: Idle comes after serving, and only then does the instance go.

prompt: Match each part of the contract to who keeps it.
hint: Left of the line is Google, right of it is you.
right_distractors: The Docker daemon on your laptop

prompt: A developer counts page views in a global variable of the service and the number on the dashboard keeps jumping backwards. Why?
hint: How many copies hold that variable?

choices.text: Python integers overflow and wrap around
choices.why: Python integers do not overflow.

choices.text: Cloud Run resets globals on every request
choices.why: Globals live as long as the instance.

choices.text: Each instance has its own counter, and instances come and go
choices.why: Right. The dashboard shows whichever instance answered.

choices.text: The counter is written to /tmp, which Cloud Run cleans each hour
choices.why: Nothing cleans /tmp hourly; the instance itself goes away.

prompt: By default, how many minutes may a Cloud Run request take before it times out?
hint: It can be raised to sixty.

prompt: The time a request waits while Cloud Run pulls the image and starts the container is the cold ___.
hint: Lesson 11 takes it apart.

prompt: Which of these would make the orders service fail Cloud Run's default startup probe?
hint: The probe opens a TCP connection to PORT.

choices.text: Hard-coding port 8000 while PORT says 8080
choices.why: Right. The probe connects to PORT and finds nothing.

choices.text: Answering /health with a 404 and a JSON body
choices.why: The default probe is TCP; it never asks for /health.

choices.text: Logging in plain text instead of JSON lines
choices.why: Log format does not affect the probe.

choices.text: Running as the user nobody
choices.why: Ports above 1024 need no root.
